entities.summary: Lucius Aurelius Orestes was a Roman magistrate and consul who played a significant role in the governance of Rome during the late Republic period. He was consul in 157 BC, serving alongside Sextus Julius Caesar, and was later mentioned in the Roman Fasti and by Gaius Plinius Secundus in his work Historia Naturalis. Orestes' tenure as consul reflects the complex power struggles and shifting alliances that characterized the late Roman Republic, as the city's elite vied for influence and control. His legacy as a magistrate and consul serves as a reminder of the Roman Republic's tumultuous final decades, marked by civil wars, foreign invasions, and the eventual rise of the Roman Empire. Despite his relatively minor status, Orestes' involvement in the Roman Republic's governance underscores the importance of understanding the intricate web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that defined this pivotal era in Roman history.
